claude_subagent.description: Claude Code workflow subagent (strongest Claude model in the session, effort high). Runs many packages in parallel inside workflows/build_dag.js, no quota problem observed. Reviewer agents are the same model family, so reviewer and implementer share blind spots. Last resort of the engine chain (after local Qwen): never quota-probed, always available.

agy_claude_opus.description: agy CLI on the newest Claude Opus that `agy models` lists ("auto:claude-opus", effort suffix in the id). Observed: ~11 min per package, ~2 confirmed defects, but quota exhausts after ~2 runs and stalls ~90 minutes. Same family as the Claude reviewers. Shares one Claude quota bucket with every other agy Claude engine (state file key agy_claude).

agy_gemini_pro.description: agy CLI on the newest Gemini that `agy models` lists ("auto:gemini", resolved per probe/run; the key name predates the Pro retirement on 2026-10-16). Track record below is from gemini-3.1-pro-high: Observed: ~6 min per package, each package tends to need one fix round with 4-9 confirmed defects (spec-literal misses: missing validators, stubbed functions, weakened tests). Different model family from the reviewers, so its errors get caught rather than shared.

codex_astra.description: OpenAI Codex CLI on gpt-6-astra, effort high, can spawn its own subagents. Usage limits hit easily; third model family, useful diversity for review-heavy or late packages.

ollama_qwen.description: Local Qwen 3.8 27B (MLX) on Ollama, driven by the Codex CLI (--oss). Free, private, never quota-limited; only where Ollama runs (the Mac; elsewhere its probe fails and the chain skips it). Slow: codex sends ~140k tokens of context, so even a trivial package takes several minutes, and a 27B model is weaker than the cloud engines on multi-file work. In the chain after Codex and before the Claude subagent, so it takes work before Claude quota is spent; best for small, fully specified packages. Runners wait up to ~140 min for it.
